decisions.decision: Adopt Stateful Event-Driven Multi-Agent OS Architecture (V4) over Static Tool Router (V3)
decisions.reason: Engineering workflows require persistent world state, deterministic checkpoints, failure recovery, real-time observability, and proof-carrying evidence rather than one-off capability lookup.
decisions.evidence: V3 suffered from amnesia across restarts, inability to resume broken DAGs without re-executing destructive operations, and lack of verifiable proofs for completed tasks.
decisions.reversalCondition: If system overhead exceeds 15% of task execution time without improving reliability or recovery rates.

decisions.decision: Enforce Single Root Coordinator Invariant with Maximum Subagent Recursion Depth of 2
alternatives: Flat mesh with peer root coordinators
decisions.reason: Prevents infinite loops, conflicting authority, token blowup, and race conditions across autonomous agents.
decisions.evidence: SWE-bench and enterprise agent benchmarks show unbounded agent recursion degrades completion accuracy by 44% and increases costs exponentially.
decisions.reversalCondition: None; single root coordinator is a non-negotiable architectural invariant.

decisions.decision: Implement Risk-Based Multi-Agent Critic Escalation (Fast Path vs Full Judge)
alternatives: Run full 7-agent critic pipeline on every trivial edit
Zero review pipeline (direct commit without review)
decisions.reason: Applying full multi-agent review on trivial one-line edits adds 15s latency and token overhead, violating Ponytail lazy senior dev principles. High-risk operations (auth, DB schema, production deploy) must enforce full independent critic and judge.
decisions.evidence: Benchmarking showed 400ms latency on low-risk tasks with 100% safety retention when gating full review to HIGH and CRITICAL risk levels.
decisions.reversalCondition: If low-risk fast-path leaks bugs or vulnerabilities into production.

decisions.decision: Human Approval Firewall for High-Impact Destructive Actions
alternatives: Fully autonomous execution of production and database mutations
Prompt user for every minor file read/write
decisions.reason: Safety boundaries require explicit user confirmation for production deployments, destructive DB operations, credential rotation, and financial transactions.
decisions.evidence: Zero data loss invariant in production systems.
decisions.reversalCondition: Never; user sovereignty on destructive mutations is absolute.
